findings.title: Federated recovery codes are sent and may be stored in plaintext, losing hashed model data
findings.body: The local path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, whose codes are hashed, together with its user label and generation time. The federated path instead serializes the raw generatedCodes list into UserCredentialModel. A user-storage provider that stores the challenge response as received therefore persists usable recovery codes in plaintext, so compromise of the external store exposes all unused codes. The label and generated-at values contained in credentialModel are also not transmitted. Send the hashed credential data/model in a defined format, or explicitly require and demonstrate hashing by the storage provider, rather than handing over the raw code list.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is not removed
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential now prefers a federated credential, but when allCodesUsed() is true this code calls removeStoredCredentialById(), which removes a locally stored credential and does not delete a credential held by user storage. The exhausted federated credential therefore remains configured for the user; although a required action is added, if that action is not completed the dead credential remains and subsequent recovery-code login can again select it instead of a valid local credential.

findings.title: Login bean crashes when the selected federated credential has no unused code
findings.body: The bean now selects a federated credential first and unconditionally calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If that federated credential is present but all its codes are used (which can happen because the authenticator cannot remove federated credentials via removeStoredCredentialById), getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() is empty and this throws NoSuchElementException, breaking rendering of the login form instead of treating the user as having no usable recovery credential or forcing regeneration.

findings.title: Test user-storage validator does not consume used recovery codes
findings.body: isValid() returns true whenever the submitted code matches any code in the stored JSON list, but it never removes or marks that code as used. Consequently the same recovery code can be replayed for unlimited logins for federated users in this provider, unlike local recovery codes which are single-use. The new test logs in only once, so this replay behaviour is not detected; update the stored credential to consume the matched code (and add a reuse-fails test).

findings.title: getCredentials can NPE and returns a credential without the stored id or label
findings.body: getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without the null check used by isConfiguredFor(), so it can throw NullPointerException for a user absent from the map. When a user is present, RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) builds a fresh model from the raw codes, created date and (always unset) user label, discarding recoveryCodesModel.getId() and getUserLabel(); callers that rely on a stable credential id (display, deletion, removal when exhausted) therefore receive a null/ephemeral id and lose the label.
